senses.definition: (historical numismatics, slang) The franc germinal: a 20-franc gold coin issued under Napoleon I of France.
(historical numismatics, slang) Other subsequent 20-franc coins, notes, or values.

quotes.text: We had occasion some months ago to strengthen our resources, and borrowed, for that purpose, thirty thousand napoleons from the Bank of France.
quotes.reference: 1891, Arthur Conan Doyle, The Adventure of the Red-Headed League, Norton, published 2005, page 67:

senses.definition: (usually admiringly derogatory) A person resembling Napoleon Bonaparte, (usually) in having come to dominate an area or sphere of activity through ruthlessness or illegality as well as surpassing ability.

quotes.text: He [sc. James Moriarty] is the Napoleon of crime, Watson. He is the organizer of half that is evil and of nearly all that is undetected in this great city [sc. London]. He is a genius, a philosopher, an abstract thinker.
quotes.reference: 1894, Arthur Conan Doyle, The Memoirs of Sherlock Holmes, page 260:

quotes.text: He [sc. McKinley] has been called the Napoleon of protection, as other men have been called Napoleons of finance.
quotes.reference: 1896, J.S. Ogilvie, The Life and Speeches of William McKinley:

senses.definition: (fashion, obsolete) Clipping of Napoleon boot, a form of topboot worn by officers during the Napoleonic Wars.

quotes.text: Always an eloquent speaker, Polk became known as the Napoleon of the stump.
quotes.reference: 2011, Robert Morgan, Lions of the West::

senses.definition: (historical weaponry) Clipping of Napoleon gun, a 12-pounder cannon first used by the Second French Empire.
(card games, uncountable) A 19th-century five-card trick-taking game simplified from euchre.
(card games, uncountable) Clipping of double napoleon, a form of patience/solitaire.
(rare UK horse racing slang, obsolete) Alternative form of nap: a horse to go nap on, a sure thing, a certain winner; a prediction of such a horse; a bet on such a horse.
Clipping of Napoleon bigarreau, a variety of the white-fleshed bigarreau cherry; a variety of cherry tree bearing such fruit.
(food, originally US slang) Clipping of Napoleon cake, another name for a millefeuille pastry.

quotes.text: Fascinated, Miss Manvers thrust aside a garnished plate, took a gulp of the decoction called coffee, and attacked her napoleon.
quotes.reference: 1914 November, Louis Joseph Vance, “An Outsider […]”, in Munsey’s Magazine, volume LIII, number II, New York, N.Y.: The Frank A[ndrew] Munsey Company, […], published 1915, →OCLC, chapter I (Anarchy), page 373, column 1:

senses.definition: (rare) Clipping of Napoleon brandy, any excellent brandy; a serving of such a brandy.
